name: Cymbals
group: Things people make > Toys > Make music with it > Hit it to make sound

features.claim: A cymbal is a thin, round plate.
features.quote: Often used in pairs, cymbals consist of thin, normally round plates of various copper alloys.
They are discs made of copper, bronze or a special alloy.

features.claim: There is a hole drilled in the center of the cymbal.
features.quote: A hole is drilled in the center of the cymbal, which is used to either mount the cymbal on a stand or for tying straps through (for hand playing).

features.claim: The bell is the raised part right around the hole.
features.quote: The bell, dome, or cup is the raised section immediately surrounding the hole.

features.claim: The bow is the rest of the surface around the bell.
features.quote: The bow is the rest of the surface surrounding the bell.

features.claim: The edge is the outer rim of the cymbal.
features.quote: The edge or rim is the immediate circumference of the cymbal.

features.claim: In the middle the cymbal juts out a little and has straps that pass through a hole.
features.quote: They look rather like saucepan lids, but in the middle they jut out a little and they have straps there that pass through a hole.

features.claim: Cymbals come in different sizes, from about 25 cm across to about 60 cm across.
features.quote: Some may be just 25 cm across, large ones may be up to 60 cm across.

features.claim: A pair of cymbals is held by a strap set in the bell of each one.
features.quote: Orchestral clash cymbals are traditionally used in pairs, each one having a strap set in the bell of the cymbal by which they are held.
